title: Radio Broadcasting
description: Documented public information: radio broadcasting — AM, FM, and digital radio — transmits audio via modulated electromagnetic waves to receivers. Documented history: from Marconi-era wireless telegraphy through 1920s broadcast radio to modern digital standards (DAB, HD Radio). A foundational documented signal use: one-to-many communication over the air.
how_it_works: Audio modulates a carrier wave (amplitude for AM, frequency for FM); receivers demodulate it back to sound. Transmitters, antennas, and allocated spectrum (regulated by bodies like the FCC/ITU) complete the system.
applications: News, music, emergency alerts, community radio — documented worldwide.

title: Television Broadcasting
description: Documented public information: television broadcasting transmits video and audio via radio-frequency signals — historically analog (NTSC/PAL/SECAM), now digital (ATSC, DVB). Documented history: 20th-century broadcast TV to digital switchover (US completed 2009).
how_it_works: Video/audio encoded, modulated onto RF carriers, transmitted from towers or satellites; receivers decode. Digital standards compress via MPEG-family codecs.
applications: Broadcast TV, public broadcasting, emergency alert systems — documented.

title: Mobile Telephony (Cellular)
description: Documented public information: cellular networks divide regions into cells, each served by a base station; phones communicate via radio signals. Documented generations: 1G (analog) through 5G (modern), with documented standards by 3GPP. The dominant documented signal use of the modern era.
how_it_works: Phones transmit/receive on licensed spectrum to nearby base stations; the network routes calls/data; handoffs maintain connections across cells.
applications: Voice, SMS, mobile internet — documented billions of users.

title: WiFi Networking
description: Documented public information: WiFi (IEEE 802.11 standards family) provides wireless local-area networking on unlicensed spectrum (2.4/5/6 GHz bands). Documented history: 1997 first standard through WiFi 6/6E/7. A foundational documented signal use: local wireless internet access.
how_it_works: Access points and devices exchange packet data via modulated radio on unlicensed bands; standards define modulation, channels, and protocols.
applications: Home/office internet, public hotspots, IoT — documented worldwide.

title: Radar
description: Documented public information: radar (radio detection and ranging) transmits radio pulses and analyzes reflections to detect objects’ distance, speed, and direction. Documented history: developed through the 1930s, decisive in WWII, now ubiquitous. Documented uses: air traffic control, weather radar, automotive radar, military (public knowledge).
how_it_works: Transmitter emits pulses; reflections return with delay (distance) and Doppler shift (speed); signal processing builds the picture.
applications: Aviation, meteorology, automotive safety, maritime navigation — documented.

title: Weather Radar
description: Documented public information: weather radar (e.g., the US NEXRAD network) detects precipitation via reflected signals. Documented: Doppler capability reveals storm motion and rotation — the basis of tornado warnings in documented meteorology.
how_it_works: Pulses reflect off precipitation; return strength indicates intensity, Doppler shift indicates motion toward/away.
applications: Storm tracking, aviation weather, public warnings — documented.

title: GPS and Satellite Navigation
description: Documented public information: GPS (US), Galileo (EU), GLONASS, BeiDou — satellite constellations broadcasting timing signals; receivers triangulate position. Documented history: GPS operational from the 1990s; civilian access documented. A foundational documented signal use.
how_it_works: Satellites broadcast precise time signals; receivers compare arrival times from multiple satellites to compute position.
applications: Navigation, surveying, timing for networks, emergency location — documented.

title: Radio Astronomy
description: Documented public information: radio telescopes (e.g., documented facilities like the Very Large Array) detect natural radio emissions from space — pulsars, galaxies, the cosmic microwave background (documented 1965 discovery). A documented scientific signal use: listening to the universe.
how_it_works: Large antennas collect faint cosmic radio waves; sensitive receivers and processing reveal sources.
applications: Astrophysics, cosmology, SETI research (documented) — documented science.

title: MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging)
description: Documented public information: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio-frequency pulses to image soft tissues — hydrogen nuclei resonate and emit signals detected by the scanner. Documented history: Lauterbur and Mansfield’s work (Nobel 2003); clinical MRI from the 1980s. A documented medical signal use.
how_it_works: Magnetic field aligns protons; RF pulses tip them; their emitted signals encode position via gradient fields; computers reconstruct images.
applications: Brain, joint, cardiac, and cancer imaging — documented medicine.
disclaimer: General information only; medical decisions belong to qualified professionals.

title: Bluetooth
description: Documented public information: Bluetooth (IEEE 802.15.1) provides short-range wireless links for peripherals and audio. Documented history: named for Harald Bluetooth; standardized from the late 1990s. A documented signal use: personal-area networking.
how_it_works: Frequency-hopping radio on 2.4 GHz; devices pair and exchange data over short range.
applications: Headphones, keyboards, wearables, beacons — documented.

title: Satellite Communications
description: Documented public information: communications satellites relay signals between ground stations — geostationary and low-earth-orbit constellations documented (including modern LEO broadband). Documented history: Telstar (1962) to modern mega-constellations.
how_it_works: Ground stations uplink to satellites, which amplify and retransmit (transponders) to other ground points.
applications: TV distribution, remote internet, maritime/aviation links — documented.

title: RFID and NFC
description: Documented public information: RFID tags and NFC (near-field communication) use radio signals for identification and short transactions. Documented uses: inventory, access cards, contactless payment, passports. A documented industrial/commercial signal use.
how_it_works: Readers energize passive tags via radio; tags respond with identifiers; NFC adds peer modes at very short range.
applications: Logistics, retail, access control, payments — documented.

title: Emergency Alert Systems
description: Documented public information: emergency alert systems (e.g., US EAS, Wireless Emergency Alerts) broadcast warnings via radio/TV/cellular signals. Documented uses: weather emergencies, AMBER alerts, presidential messages. A documented public-safety signal use.
how_it_works: Authorized originators issue alerts; broadcasters and carriers distribute via dedicated protocols to receivers/phones.
applications: Disaster warnings, missing-person alerts — documented public safety.

title: Air Traffic Control Radar and Radio
t: Air Traffic Control Radar and Radio
description: Documented public information: ATC uses primary/secondary radar plus VHF radio voice and data links to manage airspace. Documented: secondary surveillance radar interrogates aircraft transponders. A documented safety-critical signal use.
how_it_works: Radar tracks positions; transponders reply with identity/altitude; controllers coordinate via radio.
applications: En-route and terminal air traffic management — documented.

title: Microwave Ovens (Energy Use)
description: Documented public information: microwave ovens heat food with 2.45 GHz electromagnetic energy exciting water molecules. Documented history: Raytheon’s Percy Spencer (1940s); consumer ovens from the 1960s–70s. A documented ENERGY use of signals — heating, not communication.
how_it_works: Magnetron generates microwaves; waveguide distributes them in the cavity; water/fats absorb the energy as heat.
applications: Food heating — documented in billions of homes.

title: Radio Telescopes for Spacecraft Tracking
description: Documented public information: deep-space networks (e.g., NASA’s DSN, documented) communicate with distant spacecraft via radio signals — Voyager’s documented faint signals among the weakest ever received. A documented scientific signal use.
how_it_works: Giant dishes transmit commands and receive telemetry across interplanetary distances; extreme sensitivity required.
applications: Planetary missions, deep-space science — documented.

title: WiFi Sensing (Documented Research)
description: Documented public information: researchers have documented using WiFi channel-state information for presence detection, gesture recognition, and respiration-rate estimation in research settings. Documented as research — not consumer medical devices. Included because it’s the documented factual basis his speculative concepts build on.
how_it_works: Movement perturbs WiFi multipath; analyzing channel-state information reveals motion patterns.
applications: Research prototypes; smart-home presence concepts — documented research.
status: DOCUMENTED RESEARCH — not a consumer product claim

title: Wireless Power Transfer (Documented)
description: Documented public information: wireless power — inductive charging (documented in phones/toothbrushes), resonant and RF-harvesting research — transfers energy via electromagnetic fields. Documented: Qi standard for inductive charging. A documented energy use of signals.
how_it_works: Transmitter coils create oscillating fields; receiver coils convert back to current (inductive/resonant); RF harvesting captures ambient energy at low power.
applications: Phone charging, implants research, IoT sensors — documented.
status: DOCUMENTED PUBLIC USE/RESEARCH — established where stated

title: Signal Intelligence History (Public Knowledge)
description: Documented public information: signals intelligence — intercepting communications — is publicly documented history (e.g., WWII codebreaking at Bletchley Park, documented). Included as documented historical fact about signal uses; modern capabilities are not detailed here.
how_it_works: Historical record only: interception and cryptanalysis as publicly documented.
applications: Documented history; modern practice not covered.

title: Amateur Radio
description: Documented public information: amateur ("ham") radio — licensed operators experimenting with radio communication, emergency volunteering, and technical education. Documented: emergency communications role in disasters. A documented community signal use.
how_it_works: Licensed operators use allocated bands with their own equipment; modes from Morse to digital.
applications: Emergency comms, education, experimentation — documented.

title: Optical Signals: Fiber and LiFi
description: Documented public information: fiber optics carry signals as light — the internet’s backbone (documented). LiFi (light-fidelity) research documents data via modulated LED light. Documented: fiber is established; LiFi is research/early commercial.
how_it_works: Lasers/LEDs modulate light; fiber guides it with total internal reflection; receivers decode.
applications: Internet backbone (fiber, documented); indoor optical networking research (LiFi).

title: The Database’s Scope Note
description: Scope note: this database documents PUBLIC, established signal uses — communication, sensing, navigation, science, medicine, industry, emergency. It does not cover classified systems, and its medical entries (MRI) are general information, not guidance. For his speculative concepts, see the companion Signature databases.
how_it_works: As a scope note: the documented shelf vs the speculative shelf — clearly separated.
applications: Reference: the factual ground his concepts build on.

title: Signal Uses: The Complete Map
description: Summary: signals carry voices (radio, cellular), images (TV, satellite), data (WiFi, fiber), find things (radar, GPS), see inside bodies (MRI), heat food (microwaves), warn populations (EAS), and explore the universe (radio astronomy, DSN). The documented map — complete at this level — is the factual basis for everything else in this section.
how_it_works: As a summary: the full documented landscape in one record.
applications: Reference and teaching.

title: Ways to Use Signals: Closing
description: Closing: every documented signal use — fact-checked, public, established. The database’s standing: the documented is the ground; his Signature concepts (companion databases) are the playground — and the ground is not the playground.
how_it_works: As a closing: the public shelf, complete.
applications: Reference.
